en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 2.10.
Mahantaraduka (The Great Pairs)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.

Dependent on a state with an object, a state with an object arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate with an object, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … etc.

Dependent on a state with an object, a state without an object arises by way of root condition: dependent on aggregates with objects, mind-produced matter [arises]; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ...
Dependent on a state with an object, states both with and without an object arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one aggregate with an object, three aggregates and mind-produced matter [arise] ... [etc. ... dependent on two aggregates ... [etc. ...
At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc] ...

Dependent on a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of root condition: one great primary element ... [etc] ... dependent on the great primaries, mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter.
Dependent on a state without an object, a state with an object arises by way of root condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the [heart-]base, the aggregates with an object arise.

Dependent on a state without an object, states both with objects and without objects arise by way of root condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the physical basis (vatthu), the aggregates with objects arise; dependent on the great elements, kamma-produced matter (kaṭattārūpa) arises.
Dependent on a state both with an object and without an object, a state with an object arises by way of root condition:
at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with an object and the physical basis, three aggregates arise ... [and so on] ... dependent on two aggregates ... [and so on].

Dependent on a state with an object and a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of root condition: dependent on aggregates with an object and the great primaries, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc.
… Dependent on a state with an object and a state without an object, states both with an object and without an object arise by way of root condition:
at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with an object and the [heart-]base, three aggregates [arise].
... pe ... dependent on two aggregates ... pe ... dependent on aggregates that have an object and the great primary elements, there arises kamma-produced matter.
Object Condition:

Dependent on a state with an object, a state with an object arises by way of object condition—dependent on one aggregate with an object, three aggregates arise ... pe ... dependent on two aggregates ... pe ... at the moment of rebirth-linking ... pe ...
Dependent on a state without an object, a state with an object arises by way of object-condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the [heart-]base, the aggregates with objects arise.
Dependent on a state both with and without an object, a state with an object arises by way of object-condition:
at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with an object and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise … pe … dependent on two aggregates … pe … (Abbreviated.)
In the Pure Conditionality Chapter:

nine in the root condition, three in the object condition, five in the predominance condition, three in the proximity condition, three in the contiguity condition, and [three] in the conascence condition.
Nine by mutuality, six by reciprocity, nine by dependence, three by strong-dependence, one by prenascence,
one by repetition, nine by kamma, nine by resultant, nine by nutriment, nine by faculty, nine by jhāna, nine by path,
three by association, nine by dissociation, nine by presence, three by absence, three by disappearance, and nine by non-disappearance.
2.10.1.1.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra):
Not-root (Nahetu)
Dependent on a state with an object, a state with an object arises by way of not-root condition:

dependent on one rootless aggregate with an object, three aggregates [arise] …pe… two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking …pe… dependent on doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion [arises].
Dependent on a state with an object, a state without an object arises by way of the not-root condition: dependent on rootless aggregates with an object, mind-produced matter [arises];
at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … pe … Dependent on a state with an object, states both with and without an object arise by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate with an object, three aggregates and mind-produced matter [arise] … pe … two aggregates … pe …
... pe ... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking ... pe ...
Dependent on a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of the not-root condition: one great primary ... pe ... one great primary of non-percipient beings ... pe ...

Dependent on a state without an object, a state with an object arises by way of the not-root condition: at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on the [heart-]base, the aggregates with objects arise.

Dependent on a state without an object, states both with and without objects arise by way of the not-root condition: at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on the (heart-)base, the aggregates with objects arise; dependent on the great primaries, kamma-produced matter arises.
Dependent on a state both with and without objects, a state with an object arises by way of the not-root condition:
at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with an object and the (heart-)base, three aggregates arise … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on].
Dependent on a state with an object and a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on rootless aggregates with an object and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking ...
[and so forth] ... Dependent on a state with an object and a state without an object, states both with an object and without an object arise.

Not-root condition: At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one object-possessing aggregate and the [heart] base, there arise three aggregates … two aggregates … dependent on object-possessing aggregates and the great primaries, there arises kamma-produced matter.
Not-object condition … [etc.]

Dependent on a state with an object, a state without an object arises by way of non-object condition: dependent on aggregates with objects, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ...
Dependent on a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of non-object condition. (Up to the non-percipient beings.
Dependent on a state both with and without an object, a state without an object arises by way of non-object condition: dependent on aggregates with objects ... [etc. ...
Dependent on aggregates and great primaries, there is mind-originated matter; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... (Abbreviated.
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.
Nine by way of not-root; three by way of not-object; nine by way of not-predominance; three by way of not-proximity; three by way of not-contiguity;
three by way of not-mutuality; three by way of not-strong-dependence; nine by way of not-prenascence; nine by way of not-postnascence; nine by way of not-repetition;
two by way of not-kamma; five by way of not-resultant; one by way of not-nutriment; one by way of not-faculty; two by way of not-jhāna; [none] by way of not-path.
With not-root, nine; with not-association, three; with not-dissociation, two; with not-absence, three; with not-disappearance, three. 2.10.1.1.3.
Positive-Negative Conditionality By way of root condition:
with not-object, three; with not-predominance, nine ... pe ... with not-kamma, one ... pe ... with not-dissociation, one. (Abbreviated.)
2.10.1.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma):

With non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are three [results] in the object condition (ārammaṇa) … pe … nine in the conascence condition (sahajāta) … pe … one in the path condition (magga) … pe … nine in the non-disappearance condition (avigata). 2.10.1.2.
Chapter on Conascence (Sahajātavāra)
The "Co-nascent" section is also similar to the "Dependent" section.
2.10.1.3. Condition Section. 2.10.1.3.1.
Positive Conditions (Paccayānuloma).
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition. Conditioned by a state with an object, a state with an object arises by way of root condition... three. (The same as in the Paṭicca [Dependent] Chapter.)

Conditioned by a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of root condition: one great primary element … [and so on] … conditioned by the great primary elements, mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise.

Conditioned by a state without an object, a state with an object arises by way of root condition: conditioned by the [heart-]base, the aggregates with an object arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking, conditioned by the base, the aggregates with an object arise.
Conditioned by a state without an object, states both with an object and without an object arise by way of root condition: conditioned by the base … [and so on] … by way of root condition.
Conditioned by [mental] aggregates with an object, [arise] mind-produced matter conditioned by the great primaries; at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe….
Conditioned by a state both with an object and without an object, a state with an object arises by way of root condition:
conditioned by one aggregate with an object and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise …pe… conditioned by two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe….

Conditioned by a state with an object and a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of root condition: conditioned by aggregates with an object and the great primaries, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc.
… Conditioned by a state with an object and a state without an object, states both with an object and without an object arise by way of root condition:
conditioned by one aggregate with an object and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise … [etc. … conditioned by two aggregates … [etc. …
And ... [as before] ... conditioned by aggregates with an object and the great elements, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [as before] .... Object Condition:

Conditioned by a state with an object, a state with an object arises by way of object condition—conditioned by one aggregate with an object, three aggregates arise ... [as before] ... two aggregates ... [as before] ... at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [as before] ....
Conditioned by a state without an object, a state with an object arises by way of object condition:
conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises … pe … conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises; conditioned by the [heart-]base, the aggregates with an object arise;
at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … .
Conditioned by a state with an object and a state without an object, a state with an object arises by way of object-condition:

conditioned by one aggregate accompanied by eye-consciousness and the eye-base, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] … [conditioned by] one aggregate accompanied by body-consciousness … [and so on] … conditioned by one aggregate with an object and the [heart-]base,
three aggregates arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on].
… pe … At the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … (Abbreviated.
Chapter on Enumeration:
Pure.

In the case of root-cause condition (hetu-paccaya), there are nine; in object condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), three; in predominance condition (adhipati-paccaya), nine; in proximity condition (anantara-paccaya), three; in contiguity condition (samanantara-paccaya), three;

in co-nascence condition (sahajāta-paccaya), nine; in mutuality condition (aññamañña-paccaya), six; in dependence condition (nissaya-paccaya), nine; in decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya), three; in prenascence condition (purejāta-paccaya), three; in repetition condition (āsevana-paccaya), three;

in kamma condition (kamma-paccaya), nine; in resultant condition (vipāka-paccaya), nine; in nutriment condition (āhāra-paccaya), nine; in faculty condition (indriya-paccaya), nine; in jhāna condition (jhāna-paccaya), nine; in path condition (magga-paccaya), nine; in association condition (sampayutta-paccaya), [three].
Three [conditions] for dissociation, nine for presence, three for absence, three for disappearance, and nine for non-disappearance.
2.10.1.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions.
Conditioned by a state with an object that lacks a cause, a state with an object arises by way of the not-root condition... three [cases]. (The same as in the "Dependent" section.

conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises …pe… conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness arises; conditioned by the [heart-]base, rootless aggregates with an object arise;
at the moment of rebirth-linking …pe… conditioned by the [heart-]base, delusion accompanied by doubt or accompanied by restlessness arises.

Conditioned by the great primary elements, kamma-produced matter

Conditioned by one aggregate and the eye-base, three aggregates [arise] …pe… conditioned by two aggregates …pe… [conditioned by] that which is accompanied by body-consciousness …pe… conditioned by one rootless aggregate with an object and the [heart-]base,
three aggregates [arise] …pe… conditioned by two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking …pe… [conditioned by] those accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Conditioned by the aggregates and the physical basis, there arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Conditioned by both an object-possessing and a non-object-possessing state, a non-object-possessing state arises by way of the not-root condition:
conditioned by rootless object-possessing aggregates and the great primary elements, mind-produced matter arises; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... pe ... .

conditioned by one rootless aggregate with an object and the [heart-]base,
three aggregates arise … two aggregates … conditioned by rootless aggregates with an object and the great primaries, mind-originated [matter arises].

there arise three aggregates … two aggregates … conditioned by rootless object-possessing aggregates and the great primaries,
there arises kamma-produced materiality … (Abbreviated.)

2.10.1.3.3. Positive-Negative Conditionality (Paccayānulomapaccanīya) With root condition (hetupaccaya), there are three [results] in the case of non-object condition (na-ārammaṇa); nine in the case of non-predominance condition (na-adhipati) ... pe ... one in the case of non-kamma condition (na-kamma) ... pe ... one in the case of non-dissociation condition (na-vippayutta). (Abbreviated. 2.10.1.3.4. Negative-Positive Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma)
With non-root condition: three for object, three for proximity, three for contiguity, nine for conascence ... [etc. ... three for path ... nine for non-disappearance. 2.10.1.4.

A state with an object is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state with an object: roots with an object are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ...

A state with an object is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state without an object: roots with an object are a condition, by way of root-condition, for mind-produced matter; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ...
A state with an object is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state both with an object and without an object:
roots with an object are a condition, by way of root-condition, for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [and so forth].
Object with an object is a condition for a state with an object by way of object-condition:
having performed an act of giving … precept … or the observance-day duty (uposathakamma), one reviews it, enjoys it, and delights in it; taking that as an object, lust [arises].
...arises ... sorrow arises; having emerged from previously well-practiced [states] ... from jhānas ...
from noble paths, they review the path, they review the fruit, they know the defilements abandoned ...
the defilements suppressed ... the defilements formerly practiced; they [review] the aggregates with objects as impermanent ... sorrow arises.
It arises; by means of the knowledge of penetration of minds (*cetopariyañāṇa*), one knows the mind of one possessing a mind with an object:

the base of infinite space [is related] to the base of infinite consciousness …pe… the base of nothingness [is related] to the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception …pe… the aggregates with an object [are related] to the knowledge of the modes of psychic power (*iddhividhañāṇa*), the knowledge of penetration of minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa*), and the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance according to karma (*yathākammūpagañāṇa*).
[The state] without an object is related to knowledge of the future and to adverting by way of object-condition.
A state without an object is related to a state with an object by way of object-condition: the Noble Ones review Nibbāna;
Nibbāna is related to change-of-lineage, purification, the Path, the Fruition, and to adverting by way of object-condition.
Condition: The eye ... [and so on] ... the physical basis is contemplated as impermanent ... [and so on] ... sorrow arises;
one sees a visible form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear-element. The visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ...

the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the aggregates without an object are conditions for the knowledge of the various supernormal powers (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of recollecting past lives (*pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa*), and [the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings].
Knowledge of the future is related to advertence by way of object-condition.
Dominance:
A state with an object is related to a state with an object by way of dominance-condition—namely, object-dominance.
Co-nascent predominance. Object-predominance: having performed an act of giving, virtue, or the observance of the Uposatha, one regards it with esteem, reviews it, relishes it, and delights in it;
through regarding it with esteem, lust arises, wrong view arises. [Or] regarding former well-performed deeds...
Having emerged from jhāna, one regards the jhāna... The Noble Ones, having emerged from the Path, [regard the Path...]
Taking the Path as estimable, ... pe ... taking the Fruit as estimable, ... pe ... having taken the aggregates with an object as estimable, one relishes and delights in them;
with that as estimable, lust arises and wrong view arises. Conascence-predominance:
predominance with an object is a condition, by way of the predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates.

A state with an object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state without an object. Conascence-predominance: a predominance with an object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for mind-produced matter.
A state with an object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for both a state with an object and a state without an object. Conascence-predominance:
a predominance with an object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the associated aggregates and mind-produced matter.

Form is a condition for [mental states] by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). A state without an object is a condition for a state with an object by way of predominance-condition. Object-predominance:
the Noble Ones, holding Nibbāna as estimable, review it; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhu*), purification (*vodāna*), the Path (*magga*), and the Fruit (*phala*).
It is a condition by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*): taking the eye ... [and so on] ... the physical basis (*vatthu*) as estimable, one relishes it and delights in it;
taking that as estimable, lust arises and wrong view arises. [This applies to] the immediate and subsequent conditions (*anantarādi*).
A state with an object is a condition for a state with an object by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*):
preceding states with objects ... [etc. ... are a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of proximity-condition; ... by way of contiguity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*) ...
one ... by way of co-nascence-condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*) ... seven [factors] (as in the co-nascence section of the *Paṭiccasamuppādavāra*) ... by way of mutuality-condition (*aññamañña-paccaya*).
Condition ... six (the same as mutual condition in the section on "dependent") ... condition by way of support-condition ... seven.

Decisive Support (upanissaya).

A state with an object is a condition for a state with an object by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support …pe…. As natural decisive support:
relying on faith (saddhā), one gives a gift …pe… arouses conceit (māna), adopts wrong view (diṭṭhi). [One relies on] virtue …pe… wisdom (paññā), lust (rāga) …pe… aspiration (patthanā).
Physical pleasure … physical pain: depending on physical pain as a decisive support, one gives a gift … pe … one attains meditative absorption;
one kills a living being … pe … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Faith … pe … wisdom, lust … pe … aspiration, physical pleasure … physical pain:
[these] are related to faith … pe … to wisdom, to lust … pe … to aspiration, and to physical pleasure … [and so forth].
[It is] a condition for pleasure, bodily pain, the path, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state without an object is a condition for a state with an object by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [as before] … Natural decisive support:
having relied upon climate, food, and lodging, one gives a gift.
... [gives] ... [and so on] ... gives rise to attainment; kills a living being ... [and so on] ... causes a schism in the Saṅgha.

Temperature, food, and lodging are related to faith ... [and so on] ... to aspiration, bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the Path, and the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).

Taking [these] as an object, lust arises … [and so on] … grief arises;

[they reflect upon] things well-done in the past … having emerged from jhāna, they reflect upon the jhāna … the Noble Ones, having emerged from the path, reflect upon the path, reflect upon the fruit.

The aggregates associated with the mind are contemplated as impermanent … [and so on] … grief arises. By means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, they know the mind of one possessing mind-associates.

The knowledge of rebirths according to one’s kamma, the knowledge of future existences, and adverting are related to [their respective objects] by way of object condition.
A state dissociated from consciousness is related to a state associated with consciousness by way of object condition:
the Noble Ones review Nibbāna; Nibbāna is related to change-of-lineage, purification, the Path, the Fruition, and adverting.

Aggregates dissociated from consciousness are related to the knowledge of the modes of psychic power, the knowledge of recollecting past lives, the knowledge of future states,

Section on Enumeration.
In the pure cause condition there are three; in the object condition, nine; in the predominance condition, nine; in the proximity condition, nine; in the contiguity condition, nine;

in the conascence condition, nine; in the mutuality condition, nine; in the support condition, nine; in the decisive support condition, nine; in the prenascence condition, three; in the postnascence condition, three.

In the case of repetition, nine; in the case of kamma, three; in the case of result, nine; in the case of nutriment, nine; in the case of faculty, nine; in the case of jhāna, three; in the case of path, three;

in the case of association, five; in the case of dissociation, nine; in the case of presence, nine; in the case of absence, nine; in the case of disappearance, nine; in the case of non-disappearance, nine. This is the direct order (anuloma).

Dependent on the great primary elements, derived matter consisting of kamma-produced form [arises]. In the case of non-percipient beings, dependent on one great primary element … [and so on] … dependent on the great primary elements, derived matter consisting of kamma-produced form [arises].
Dependent on a clung-to state, a non-clung-to state arises by way of not-object condition: dependent on the clung-to aggregates, mind-originated matter [arises].
Dependent on a state not acquired by clinging, a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of not-object condition:

dependent on aggregates not acquired by clinging, mind-produced matter; one great primary element … [and so on] … external … nutriment-produced … one great primary element produced by temperature … [and so on] … dependent on great primaries, derived matter.

Dependent on both acquired (*upādinna*) and non-acquired (*anupādinna*) states, a non-acquired state arises by way of the condition of not-object (*na-ārammaṇa-paccaya*): dependent on the acquired aggregates and the great elements (*mahābhūta*), mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) arises.
Not-predominance, etc.:

Dependent on an acquired state, an acquired state arises by way of the condition of not-predominance (*na-adhipati-paccaya*) … not-proximity (*na-anantara-paccaya*) … not-contiguity (*na-samanantara-paccaya*) … not-mutuality (*na-aññamañña-paccaya*) … not-strong-dependence (*na-upanissaya-paccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is clung-to (*upādinna*) by way of not-prenascence condition (*napurejāta-paccaya*), a state that is clung-to arises: in the immaterial plane,
dependent on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking (*paṭisandhi-kkhaṇa*), [dependent on] a clung-to [aggregate].
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-produced matter arise … dependent on two aggregates … (continue) … up to the non-percipient beings.
A clung-to state arises dependent on a clung-to state by way of not-prenascence condition: dependent on the clung-to aggregates, mind-originated matter arises.
A state not clung-to arises dependent on a state not clung-to by way of not-prenascence condition: in the immaterial plane …

Dependent on one aggregate not acquired by clinging (*anupādinnam*), three aggregates arise … [and so on] … two aggregates … [and so on] … dependent on aggregates not acquired by clinging, mind-originated matter arises;
one great primary element … [and so on] … (up to non-percipient beings).

Dependent on a state both acquired by clinging and not acquired by clinging, a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of the not-prenascence condition (*napurejātapaccaya*): dependent on [aggregates] acquired by clinging … [and so on].
Dependent on aggregates and great elements, mind-produced matter [arises]... not by way of postnascence condition... not by way of repetition condition.
Not-by-way-of-kamma:
Dependent on a state not acquired by clinging, a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of not-kamma condition—dependent on [states] not acquired by clinging...
Volition not acquired by clinging dependent on the aggregates; external [matter]; matter produced by nutriment; matter produced by temperature...
dependent on the great elements, derived matter.
Not-resultant.

Dependent on a state that is clung-to (*upādinna*), a state that is clung-to arises by way of the non-resultant condition (*navipākapaccaya*): one great primary element (*mahābhūta*) of non-percipient beings … [and so on] … dependent on the great primaries, there arise kamma-produced matter (*kaṭattārūpa*) and derived matter (*upādārūpa*).
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to, a state that is not clung-to arises by way of the non-resultant condition:
dependent on one aggregate (*khandha*) that is not clung-to, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise … [and so on] … two aggregates … [and so on].
One great primary element … [and so on] … (up to temperature-originated).

Conditioned by a state that is clung-to and not derived from nutriment, a state that is clung-to arises by way of the condition of non-nutriment: one great primary element of non-percipient beings … [and so on] …

Dependent on a state not acquired by clinging (*anupādinna*), a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of non-nutriment condition (*na-āhāra-paccaya*): external [matter] ... temperature-originated matter ...
[and so forth].

Dependent on a state acquired by clinging (*upādinna*), a state acquired by clinging arises by way of non-faculty condition (*na-indriya-paccaya*): dependent on the great primary elements (*mahābhūta*) of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), the material life-faculty (*rūpa-jīvitindriya*) arises.

Dependent on a state not acquired by clinging (*anupādinna*), a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of the faculty-condition (*indriya-paccaya*): external [matter]... nutriment-produced matter... temperature-produced matter... and so forth. Without Jhāna, etc.:

Dependent on a state acquired by clinging (*upādinna*), a state acquired by clinging arises by way of the non-jhāna-condition (*najhāna-paccaya*): dependent on one aggregate accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness, three aggregates arise... two aggregates... and so forth; [also] in the case of non-percipient beings... and so forth.

Dependent on a state not acquired by clinging (*anupādinna*), a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of the condition of non-jhāna (*najhānapaccaya*): external [matter] … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … [and so forth].

Dependent on a state acquired by clinging (*upādinna*), a state acquired by clinging arises by way of the condition of non-path (*namaggapaccaya*) [similar to the condition of non-root (*nahetu*), with the exception that delusion (*moha*) is absent] … by way of the condition of non-association (*nasampayuttapaccaya*).
[The conditions of non-dissociation, etc., follow.]
Dependent on a state that is clung-to (*upādinna*), a state that is clung-to arises by way of non-dissociation condition:

in the formless realm, dependent on one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] … dependent on one great primary element (*mahābhūta*) of non-percipient beings … [and so on] ….
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to, a state that is not clung-to arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the formless realm … [and so on] ….

Dependent on one aggregate not acquired by clinging, there arise three aggregates … two aggregates … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … [and so on] … by way of non-absence condition … by way of non-disappearance condition.
Chapter on Enumeration.
In the pure [conditioning], there are five by way of not-root, four by way of not-object, five by way of not-predominance, four by way of not-proximity, four by way of not-contiguity,
four by way of not-mutuality, four by way of not-strong-dependence, four by way of not-prenascence, and four by way of not-postnascence.
Five [in the case of] not-by-repetition; five [in the case of] not-by-kamma; one [in the case of] not-resultant; two [in the case of] not-nutriment; two [in the case of] not-faculty;

two [in the case of] not-jhāna; five [in the case of] not-path; four [in the case of] not-association; two [in the case of] not-dissociation; four [in the case of] not-absence; four [in the case of] not-disappearance. 2.10.14.1.3.
Positive-Negative Conditionality (Paccayānulomapaccanīya).
With root condition, there are four [answers] for not-object; five for not-predominance …pe… four for not-prenascence;
five for not-postnascence; five for not-repetition; one for not-kamma; one for not-resultant …pe… four for not-association;
two for not-dissociation; four for not-absence; four for not-disappearance.
2.10.14.1.4. Positive Order of the Negative Conditions (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma):

With non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are two [types] in relation to object (ārammaṇa), two in relation to proximity (anantara), two in relation to contiguity (samanantara), five in relation to conascence (sahajāta), two in relation to mutuality (aññamañña), five in relation to support (nissaya), two in relation to decisive support (upanissaya), two in relation to prenascence (purejāta), one in relation to repetition (āsevana), five in relation to kamma (kamma), and [five] in relation to result (vipāka).
Five ... [and so on] ... one in the path; two in association ... [and so on] ... five in non-disappearance. 2.10.14.2.
The Section on Conascent (Sahajātavāra).
The section on the conascent is the same as the section on dependence (Paṭiccavāra).
2.10.14.3. Chapter on Conditions (Paccayavāra) 2.10.14.3.1.
Positive Analysis of Conditions (Paccayānuloma Vibhaṅgavāra)
Conditioned by a state that is grasped, a state that is grasped arises by way of the root condition: conditioned by one aggregate that is grasped,
three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking, conditioned by one aggregate that is grasped … [and so on].
Conditioned by [one] aggregate, there arise three aggregates and derived matter; ... two aggregates ... conditioned by aggregates, there arises the [heart-]base;
conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise aggregates; one great primary ... conditioned by great primaries, there arise kamma-produced matter and derived matter;
conditioned by the [heart-]base, there arise acquired aggregates.

Conditioned by a state that is clung-to (*upādinna*), a state that is not clung-to (*anupādinna*) arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*): conditioned by the clung-to aggregates, mind-produced matter (*cittasamuṭṭhāna-rūpa*) [arises]; conditioned by the physical basis (*vatthu*), the aggregates that are not clung-to [arise].

Conditioned by a state that is clung-to, states that are both clung-to and not clung-to arise by way of the root-condition: conditioned by one clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter [arise] … two aggregates … [and so on].

Conditioned by a state not acquired through clinging (*anupādinna*), a state not acquired through clinging arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*): conditioned by one aggregate not acquired through clinging,

three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] … conditioned by one great primary (*mahābhūta*) … [and so on] … conditioned by the great primaries, mind-produced derived matter (*upādārūpa*) arises.
Conditioned by both acquired (*upādinna*) and unacquired (*anupādinna*) phenomena, an unacquired phenomenon arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*):
conditioned by the acquired aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises;
conditioned by one unacquired aggregate and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise … and so on … conditioned by two aggregates … and so on …
Conditioned by a state that is clung-to, a state that is clung-to arises by way of object-condition: conditioned by one aggregate that is clung-to,
three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … at the moment of rebirth-linking … the physical basis.

Conditioned by [the six] bases, the aggregates arise; conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness arises …pe… [and so on for the other sense-bases] … conditioned by the body-base …pe… conditioned by the physical basis (vatthu), the acquired (upādinnā) aggregates arise.
Conditioned by an acquired phenomenon, a non-acquired phenomenon arises by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya): conditioned by the physical basis, the non-acquired aggregates arise.

Conditioned by a state not acquired by clinging (*anupādinna*), a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of object condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*): conditioned by one aggregate not acquired by clinging, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … [and so on].

Conditioned by a state both acquired and not acquired by clinging, a state not acquired by clinging arises by way of object condition: conditioned by one aggregate not acquired by clinging and the [heart-]base, three aggregates [arise] … two aggregates … [and so on].
Predominance (*adhipati*).

Conditioned by a state that is clung-to (*upādinna*), a state that is not clung-to (*anupādinna*) arises by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*): conditioned by the [heart-]base, the aggregates that are not clung-to arise.
Conditioned by a state that is not clung-to, a state that is not clung-to arises by way of the predominance condition:
conditioned by one aggregate that is not clung-to, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … pe … conditioned by two aggregates … pe …
One great primary element … [and so on] … conditioned by the great primary elements, mind-originated matter and derived matter arise.
Conditioned by states that are both clung-to and not-clung-to, a state that is not-clung-to arises by way of predominance condition:
conditioned by one aggregate that is not-clung-to and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on]. (Abbreviated.)
In the pure cause section of the Enumeration Chapter:
five in the object condition, three in the predominance condition, four in the proximity condition, and four in the contiguity condition.
In co-nascence there are five; in mutuality, four; in dependence, five; in decisive support, four; in prenascence, four;
in repetition, three; in kamma, five; in result, five … pe … in non-disappearance, five.
2.10.14.2. Negative Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīya)
Vibhaṅgavāra:
Conditioned by a state that is not a root and is clung-to (upādinna), a state that is clung-to arises by way of the not-root condition (nahetupaccaya)— namely, a rootless state that is clung-to.

Conditioned by one aggregate, three aggregates arise …pe… conditioned by two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking …pe… conditioned by the aggregates, the [heart-]base arises; conditioned by the base, the aggregates arise;
one great primary …pe… conditioned by the great primaries, kamma-produced derived matter arises; in the case of non-percipient beings, one great primary …pe… the eye-base.
Conditioned by [the sense bases], eye-consciousness arises …pe… the body-base …pe… conditioned by the physical basis (vatthu), rootless (ahetuka) clung-to (upādinnā) aggregates arise.
Conditioned by a clung-to state, a non-clung-to state arises by way of the not-root condition:
conditioned by rootless clung-to aggregates, mind-produced matter arises; conditioned by the physical basis, rootless non-clung-to aggregates arise.
Conditioned by a [mental] basis, there arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Conditioned by a state that is clung-to, states that are both clung-to and not clung-to arise by way of the not-root condition:
conditioned by one rootless clung-to aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … [and so on] … conditioned by two aggregates … [and so on] …
Conditioned by a state not grasped at (anupādinna), a state not grasped at arises by way of the not-root condition (nahetupaccaya):

conditioned by one rootless aggregate not grasped at, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise … two aggregates … one great primary element … external … nutriment-produced … temperature-produced … [and] associated with doubt.
Conditioned by aggregates associated with restlessness, arises delusion associated with doubt and associated with restlessness.
Conditioned by states that are both clung-to and not-clung-to, a state that is not-clung-to arises by way of the not-root condition:
conditioned by rootless clung-to aggregates and great primaries, there arises mind-produced matter; [and] the rootless not-clung-to...

Conditioned by one aggregate and the [heart-]base, three aggregates arise …pe… conditioned by two aggregates …pe… conditioned by the doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied aggregates and the [heart-]base, doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied delusion arises. (Abbreviated.
Section on Enumeration.
Pure: five by not-root, four by not-object, five by not-predominance, four by not-proximity, four by not-contiguity,
four by not-mutuality, four by not-strong-dependence, four by not-prenascence, four by not-postnascence.
Five [in the case of] not-by-repetition; five [in the case of] not-by-kamma; three [in the case of] not-by-resultant; four [in the case of] not-by-nutriment; two [in the case of] not-by-faculty;
two [in the case of] not-by-jhāna; two [in the case of] not-by-path; five [in the case of] not-by-association; four [in the case of] not-by-dissociation; two [in the case of] not-by-absence;

2.10.14.3.4. Positive Order of the Negative Condition (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma):

With the non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are four [results] in the object condition (ārammaṇa), four in the proximity condition (anantara) … pe … three in the path condition (magga) … pe … five in the non-disappearance condition (avigata).
2.10.14.4. Section on Support (Nissayavāra)
The Section on Dependence (Nissayavāra) is similar to the Section on Conditions (Paccayavāra). 2.10.14.5.
The Section on Conjoined Relations (Saṃsaṭṭhavāra):
2.10.14.5.1–4. Positive Conditions, etc. (Paccayānulomādi).

A clung-to state arises in association with a clung-to state by way of root condition: three aggregates arise in association with one clung-to aggregate … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].
A non-clung-to state arises in association with a non-clung-to state by way of root condition: three aggregates arise in association with one non-clung-to aggregate … two aggregates … [and so on].

[In the root condition there are] two; in the object condition, two; in the predominance condition, one; in the proximity condition, two; in the contiguity condition, two; in the conascence condition … [and so on].
Two [conditions] in mutuality, two in mutuality, two in dependence, two in decisive support, two in prenascence, one in repetition, two in kamma,
two in result …pe… two in non-disappearance.
Positive.

A grasped phenomenon associated with a grasped phenomenon arises by way of the not-root condition: three aggregates associated with one rootless grasped aggregate … two aggregates … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … [and so forth].
A non-grasped phenomenon associated with a non-grasped phenomenon arises by way of the not-root condition:
three aggregates associated with one rootless non-grasped aggregate … two aggregates … [and so forth] … those accompanied by doubt.
The delusion associated with restlessness is associated with the aggregates associated with restlessness and accompanied by doubt.

[In the negative analysis: two [are absent] due to not-root; two due to not-predominance; two due to not-prenascence; two due to not-postnascence; two due to not-repetition; one due to not-kamma; one due to not-resultant; one due to not-jhāna; two due to not-path; two due to not-dissociation. The Negative Analysis is concluded.
2.10.14.6. The Section on Conjunction (Sampayuttavāra):
Thus, the other two—the Enumeration (Gaṇanā) and the Section on Conjunction—should also be performed. 2.10.14.7.
The Section of Questions (Pañhāvāra)
2.10.14.7.1. Positive Exposition of Conditions (Paccayānuloma):
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra) – Root Condition (Hetu)
A grasped state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a grasped state:

grasped roots are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates; at the moment of rebirth-linking, grasped roots are a condition, by way of root-condition, for their associated aggregates and for the kamma-produced matter.
A grasped state is a condition for a non-grasped state by way of the root-condition: grasped roots are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of the root-condition.

A grasped state is a condition for both grasped and non-grasped states by way of the root-condition: grasped roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of the root-condition.

A non-clung-to state is a condition for a non-clung-to state by way of root-condition: non-clung-to roots are a condition by way of root-condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Object-condition:
A clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of object-condition: the eye ... [and so on] ... the body.
In regard to appropriated forms … odors … tastes … tangibles … and in regard to the appropriated bases (the aggregates), [one contemplates them] as impermanent … [and so on] … grief arises;
when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, their result arises by way of object-condition (*tadārammaṇa*).
An appropriated visible-object base [arises] for eye-consciousness … an appropriated odor-base for nose-consciousness … a tangible-object base … [for body-consciousness].
[It is] a condition for body-consciousness by way of object-condition.
A clung-to state is a condition for a non-clung-to state by way of object-condition: the eye … [and so on] … the body;
[or] the clung-to visible forms … odors … tastes … tangible objects … [or] the base; [or] the clung-to aggregates, [contemplating them] as impermanent … [and so on].
Mental distress arises; one sees acquired form with the divine eye.

By means of knowledge of the penetration of minds, one knows the mind of one possessing an acquired mind. Acquired aggregates are related to the knowledge of the modes of psychic power, the knowledge of the penetration of minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of future states, and to advertence by way of object condition.
A state not acquired by clinging is a condition for a state not acquired by clinging by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*):
having performed an act of giving … precept-observance … or the observance-day duty (*uposathakamma*), one reviews it, relishes it, and delights in it;

taking that as an object, lust … or even grief arises; [or] regarding formerly well-performed deeds … meditative absorptions (*jhāna*) … or the Noble Ones, having emerged from the Path … [review them].
They review the path, the fruit, … nibbāna … nibbāna is related to change-of-lineage,
purification, the path, the fruit, and adverting by way of object-condition. Noble ones [review] abandoned defilements,
… suppressed defilements, … [the past] … non-clung-to forms, sounds, odors, tastes, and tangibles.
Through the contemplation of the aggregates not acquired by clinging as impermanent … [and so on] … grief arises;
one sees with the divine eye form not acquired by clinging, and hears sound with the divine ear-element.

Through the knowledge of penetration of minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a mind not acquired by clinging; [one knows] the base of infinite space … [and so on] … the base of nothingness … [and so on] … the aggregates not acquired by clinging [are objects] of the knowledge of the modes of psychic power.
Knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of recollecting past lives, knowledge of the destination according to kamma, knowledge of future states,
and adverting are related to [their respective objects] by way of object condition.
A state not acquired by clinging is related to a state acquired by clinging by way of object condition— namely, forms not acquired by clinging.
...in sounds ... smells ... tastes ... tangibles, and in non-clung-to aggregates, through [contemplating them] as impermanent ... pe ... sorrow arises;
when wholesome or unwholesome [states] have ceased, the resultant [consciousness] arises with that as its object; wholesome *ākāsānañcāyatana* [leads to] resultant *viññāṇañcāyatana* ...
pe ... wholesome *ākiñcaññāyatana* ... pe ... the non-clung-to visible-form base (*rūpāyatana*).

The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the sound-base ... [and so on] ... the tangible-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
Predominance:
A clung-to state is a condition for a non-clung-to state by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*). Object-predominance: the eye ... [and so on].
... pe ... [one] esteems, relishes, and delights in the body as clung-to form, in odors, in tastes, in tangibles, and in the bases as clung-to aggregates;
esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises.
A state not clung-to is a condition for a state not clung-to by way of the predominance condition: objective-predominance.
Co-nascent predominance. Object-predominance: having performed an act of giving … morality … or the observance-day ceremony, one esteems it, reviews it, relishes it, and delights in it;
through esteeming it, lust arises, wrong view arises.
Regarding the past … regarding jhānas … when Noble Ones have emerged from the path, they esteem and review the path.
They esteem and reflect upon the fruit... and Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, purification, the path, and the fruit by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
[One] esteems, relishes, and delights in unclung-to forms... sounds... odors... tastes... tangibles, and unclung-to aggregates, esteeming them as such. That [esteeming]...
Having performed [an action], lust arises; a view arises. Co-nascent predominance:
non-clung-to predominance is a condition, by way of the predominance condition, for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Immediate...
A grasped phenomenon is a condition for a grasped phenomenon by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*):
preceding grasped aggregates are a condition for subsequent grasped aggregates by way of proximity condition.

The fivefold sense-consciousness is a condition for the resultant mind-element by way of proximity condition. The resultant mind-element is [a condition] for the resultant mind-consciousness-element...
It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

A clung-to phenomenon (*upādinna-dhamma*) is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon (*anupādinna-dhamma*) by way of proximity-condition: the life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) is a condition for adverting (*āvajjana*); the resultant mind-consciousness-element (*vipāka-manoviññāṇadhātu*) is a condition for the functional mind-consciousness-element (*kiriya-manoviññāṇadhātu*) by way of proximity-condition.
A non-clung-to phenomenon is a condition for a non-clung-to phenomenon by way of proximity-condition: preceding [states]... [are conditions for] succeeding [states].
Appropriated aggregates are related to subsequent non-appropriated aggregates by way of proximity condition;
adaptation is related to change-of-lineage …pe… and fruition attainment by way of proximity condition.
A non-appropriated state is related to an appropriated state by way of proximity condition: adverting [consciousness] to the five [sense-cognitions].

For consciousnesses ... [and so on] ... the aggregates not acquired by clinging are related to emergence by way of proximity condition, contiguity condition, co-nascence condition—five [types, as in the Paṭicca-vagga]—reciprocity condition—two [types, as in the Paṭicca-vagga]—and support condition—five [types, as in the support section of the Paccaya-vāra].

A grasped state is a condition for a grasped state by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, as proximity-decisive support (anantara-upanissaya) and natural decisive support (pakata-upanissaya)… [as above]… Natural decisive support:
bodily pleasure is a condition for bodily pleasure… bodily pain... [and so forth].

[It is] a condition for suffering by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*); bodily suffering … clung-to temperature … food [is] a condition for bodily pleasure … bodily suffering by way of decisive support condition;
bodily pleasure … bodily suffering … temperature … food … [is] a condition for bodily pleasure … bodily suffering by way of decisive support condition.

A grasped state is a condition for a non-grasped state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—namely, as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support … [etc.
… Natural decisive support: relying on bodily pleasure, one gives a gift … [etc.
… one causes a schism in the Saṅgha; [or] relying on bodily pain … or a grasped temperature … or food.
One gives a gift … [and so on] … one arouses an attainment; one kills a living being … [and so on] … one causes a schism in the Saṅgha;

bodily pleasure … bodily pain … temperature … food … faith … [and so on] … aspiration is a condition for the path, for the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).
A state not acquired by clinging is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state not acquired by clinging:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support ... [etc. ... Natural decisive support:
relying on faith as a decisive support, one gives a gift, arouses conceit, or adopts a wrong view; [relying on] virtue ... aspiration ... climate ... food ... lodging.
One gives a gift depending on [something]; ... [and so on] ... one causes a schism in the Saṅgha. Faith ... aspiration ... climate ... food ...
lodging is a condition for faith ... aspiration ... the Path, and for the attainment of fruition, by way of the decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya).

A state not acquired by clinging (anupādinna) is a condition for a state acquired by clinging (upādinna) by way of the decisive support condition—namely, as immediate decisive support (anantara-upanissaya).
Natural strong-dependence … [as above] … Natural strong-dependence: depending on faith, one torments oneself and torments others, and experiences suffering rooted in searching;
depending on virtue … [and so on] … depending on aspiration, temperature, food, and lodging, one torments oneself and torments others, and experiences suffering rooted in searching.
Faith … [and so on] … lodging is related to bodily pleasure … and bodily pain by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is related to its result by way of decisive support condition.
Prenascence (*purejāta*).
A clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.

Regarding object-prenascence: the eye … [and so on] … the body; [or] in regard to clung-to forms … odors … tastes … tangibles … [or] in regard to the base, through [contemplating it as] impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises; when wholesome or unwholesome [states] have ceased … [and so on].

Resultant [matter] arises as its object-condition (*tadārammaṇa*): the clung-to visible-object base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the odor-base …pe… the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe…. Base-prenascence:

the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness …pe… the [heart-]base is a condition for the clung-to aggregates by way of prenascence-condition.
A grasped state is a condition for a non-grasped state by way of prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.

As for object-prenascence: the eye … [and so on] … the body; with regard to grasped visible forms … odors … tastes … tangible objects, and the physical base, through [contemplating them as] impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises. By means of the divine eye, that which is grasped … [is seen].
One sees a visible form. As object-prenascence: the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition by way of prenascence-condition for the aggregates not acquired through clinging.
A state not acquired through clinging is a condition by way of prenascence-condition for a state not acquired through clinging. As object-prenascence:

regarding visible forms not acquired through clinging … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles, [contemplating them] as impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises; by means of the divine [eye] … [and so on].
One sees a form not acquired by clinging with the eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element.
A state not acquired by clinging is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for a state acquired by clinging. As object-prenascence:

regarding forms not acquired by clinging … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles, [contemplating them] as impermanent … [and so on] … sorrow arises; [regarding] wholesome and unwholesome [states] … [and so on].
When [the object] has ceased, its result arises as having that as its object;
the non-clung-to visible base is a pre-arising condition for eye-consciousness … pe … the sound base … pe … the tangible base is a pre-arising condition for body-consciousness.
Both clung-to and non-clung-to states are a pre-arising condition for a clung-to state.

Object-prenascence and base-prenascence. Non-clung-to visible-object-base and eye-base are related to eye-consciousness by way of prenascence condition … sound-base and ear-base … tangible-object-base and body-base are related to body-consciousness by way of prenascence condition;
non-clung-to visible-object-base and [heart-]base … tangible-object-base and [heart-]base … [and so on].
The [material] base is a condition for the clung-to aggregates by way of the pre-arising condition (*purejātapaccaya*).
Both clung-to and unclung-to states are conditions for an unclung-to state by way of the pre-arising condition—namely, object-pre-arising (*ārammaṇapurejāta*) and base-pre-arising (*vatthupurejāta*).
The unclung-to visible-object base and the [material] base …pe… the tangible-object base and the [material] base …pe… [are conditions].
And the physical basis (vatthu) is a condition for the non-clung-to aggregates by way of the pre-nascence condition.

The subsequently-arisen associated-with-clinging state is a condition for the associated-with-clinging state by way of the post-nascence condition: the subsequently-arisen associated-with-clinging aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent associated-with-clinging body by way of the post-nascence condition.

A grasped state is a condition for a non-grasped state by way of postnascence condition: postnascent grasped aggregates are a condition for this prenascent non-grasped body by way of postnascence condition.
A grasped state is a condition for both grasped and non-grasped states by way of postnascence condition. (Abbreviated.
A non-grasped state is a condition for a non-grasped state by way of postnascence condition. (Abbreviated.)
A state not acquired by clinging is a condition for a state acquired by clinging by way of postnascence condition. (Abbreviated.
A state not acquired by clinging is a condition for a state both acquired by clinging and not acquired by clinging by way of postnascence condition. (Abbreviated.
A state not acquired by clinging is a condition for a state not acquired by clinging by way of repetition condition … one. (Abbreviated.)
Kamma:
A state acquired by clinging is related to a state acquired by clinging by way of kamma-condition.
An acquired volition is related to its associated aggregates by way of kamma-condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking, an acquired volition is related to its associated [aggregates]...
The aggregates and the matter produced by kamma are related to [their results] by way of kamma-condition.
A grasped state is related to a non-grasped state by way of kamma-condition: grasped volition is related to mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.

A grasped state is related to both a grasped and a non-grasped state by way of kamma-condition: grasped volition is related to the associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.

A non-clung-to state is a condition for a non-clung-to state by way of kamma-condition: non-clung-to volition is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.

A non-clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of kamma-condition: asynchronous non-clung-to volition is a condition for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced matter by way of kamma-condition.
Resultant...
A grasped phenomenon is a condition for a grasped phenomenon by way of resultant condition: one grasped aggregate [is a condition] for [the others].
A non-grasped phenomenon is a condition for a non-grasped phenomenon by way of resultant condition:
one non-grasped resultant aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of resultant condition.
... pe ... two aggregates ... pe ....
Nutriment:
A clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of nutriment-condition—the clung-to nutriments [are a condition] for their associated states.
The aggregates are related to the aggregates by way of nutriment condition; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [and so on] ...
the appropriated physical food is related to this appropriated body by way of nutriment condition.
An appropriated state is related to an unappropriated state by way of nutriment condition: the appropriated nutriments are related to mind-produced [matter].
Material phenomena are related to material phenomena by way of nutriment condition. Clung-to edible food is related to this unclung-to body by way of nutriment condition.
A clung-to state is related to both a clung-to and an unclung-to state by way of nutriment condition—[namely] the clung-to...
Nutriments are a condition by way of nutriment-condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter;
edible food that is clung-to is a condition by way of nutriment-condition for this body, both that which is clung-to and that which is not clung-to.
A state that is not clung-to is a condition by way of nutriment-condition for a state that is not clung-to: nutriments that are not clung-to.
A non-clung-to state is a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of nutriment-condition;
edible food that is not clung-to is a condition for this body that is not clung-to by way of nutriment-condition.
A non-clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of nutriment-condition: edible food that is not clung-to is a condition for this body that is clung-to by way of nutriment-condition.
A state not acquired by clinging (*anupādinnadhamma*) is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition (*āhārapaccaya*), for a state both acquired by clinging and not acquired by clinging:
edible food not acquired by clinging is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for this body which is both acquired by clinging and not acquired by clinging.

States both acquired by clinging and not acquired by clinging are conditions, by way of nutriment-condition, for a state acquired by clinging: edible food both acquired by clinging and not acquired by clinging is a condition, by way of nutriment-condition, for this body acquired by clinging.

States, both clung-to (*upādinna*) and not-clung-to (*anupādinna*), are a condition for a state that is not-clung-to by way of nutriment-condition (*āhāra-paccaya*): edible food, both clung-to and not-clung-to, is a condition for this body, which is not-clung-to, by way of nutriment-condition.
States, both clung-to and not-clung-to, are a condition for a state that is both clung-to and not-clung-to by way of nutriment-condition:
edible food, both clung-to and not-clung-to, is a condition for this [body] which is both clung-to and not-clung-to...
And [nutriment] is a condition for the body by way of the nutriment-condition.

A clung-to state, such as the faculties and so forth, is a condition for a clung-to state by way of the faculty-condition: the clung-to faculties are a condition for their associated aggregates by way of the faculty-condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, the acquired faculties are related to the associated aggregates and to the material phenomena produced by kamma (kaṭattā-rūpa) by way of the faculty condition.
The eye-faculty is related to eye-consciousness ... [and so on] ... the body-faculty is related to body-consciousness ... [and so on] ...
The material life-faculty is related to the material phenomena produced by kamma by way of the faculty condition.

A grasped state is related to a non-grasped state ... [etc. (In the section based on the grasped, there are three; for the first alone, the material life-faculty is included, while for the others, it is not present.

A non-grasped state is related to a non-grasped state by way of the faculty condition: non-grasped faculties are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of the faculty condition.
A grasped state is a condition for a grasped state by way of the jhāna-condition: four; by way of the path-condition: four; by way of the association-condition: two.
A grasped state is a condition for a grasped state by way of the dissociation-condition: conascent, prenascent.
Postnascent: Conascent—At the moment of rebirth-linking, the acquired aggregates are related to the kamma-produced matter by way of dissociation condition;
the aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of dissociation condition; the physical basis is related to the aggregates by way of dissociation condition.
Prenascent: The eye-base to eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the body-base to body-consciousness.
...pe... A [clung-to] base is related to clung-to aggregates by way of dissociation condition.
Postnascent clung-to aggregates are related to this prenascent clung-to body by way of dissociation condition.
A clung-to state is related to a non-clung-to state by way of dissociation condition: by way of conascence, by way of prenascence.
Postnascent: Co-nascent acquired aggregates are related to mind-produced matter by dissociation condition.
Prenascent: The physical basis is related to unacquired aggregates by dissociation condition. Postnascent:
Acquired aggregates are related to this prenascent unacquired body by dissociation condition.
A grasped phenomenon is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for both a grasped and an ungrasped phenomenon.
Subsequently arisen grasped aggregates are a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for this previously arisen body which is both grasped and ungrasped.
A not-clung-to state is a condition for a not-clung-to state by way of dissociation condition:
namely, conascence and post-nascence. Conascent not-clung-to aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of dissociation condition.
Post-nascent not-clung-to aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent not-clung-to body by way of dissociation condition.

A non-clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of dissociation-condition. Subsequently arisen non-clung-to aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen clung-to body by way of dissociation-condition.
A non-clung-to state is a condition for both a clung-to and a non-clung-to state by way of dissociation-condition.
Subsequently arisen non-clung-to aggregates are [a condition] for this previously arisen [state that is] both clung-to and non-clung-to...
It is a condition for the body by way of dissociation-condition (*vippayutta-paccaya*). Regarding the presence-condition (*atthi-paccaya*) and so forth:

a clung-to state (*upādinnadhamma*) is a condition for a clung-to state by way of presence-condition—namely, conascence (*sahajāta*), prenascence (*purejāta*), postnascence (*pacchājāta*), nutriment (*āhāra*), and faculty (*indriya*).

A grasped state is a condition for a non-grasped state by way of presence-condition: conascence, prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (Abbreviated; the listed terms should be expanded as appropriate.

A grasped state is a condition for both a grasped and a non-grasped state by way of presence-condition: conascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (Abbreviated; the listed terms should be expanded as appropriate.)

A not-clung-to state is a condition for a not-clung-to state by way of presence condition: conascent, prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment. (Abbreviated; the terms as set forth should be analyzed.
A not-clung-to state is a condition for a clung-to state by way of presence condition: prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment. Prenascence:
in regard to not-clung-to forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles, [one contemplates them] as impermanent … [and so on].
Dissatisfaction arises; when wholesome or unwholesome states have ceased, their resultant arises as an object-condition (*tadārammaṇa*).
The non-clung-to form-base is a condition for eye-consciousness … [and so on] … the tangible-base is a condition for body-consciousness … [and so on] ….
Postnascent non-clung-to aggregates are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for this prenascent clung-to body; the non-clung-to … [is a condition].
Edible food is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for this acquired body.
A non-acquired phenomenon is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for both an acquired and a non-acquired phenomenon:
as postnascence and as nutriment. Postnascent non-acquired aggregates are [conditions] for this prenascent acquired and non-acquired [body].
And [nutriment] is a condition for the body by way of presence-condition; edible food that is not clung-to is a condition for this body, both clung-to and not clung-to, by way of presence-condition.
Clung-to and not clung-to states are conditions for a clung-to state by way of presence-condition—namely, pre-arising.
Post-nascence, nutriment, and faculty. Prenascence:

the non-clung-to visible-object base and eye base are related to eye-consciousness by way of presence condition …pe… the non-clung-to tangible-object base and body base are related to body-consciousness by way of presence condition; the non-clung-to visible-object base and the [heart-]base …pe… the tangible-object base and the [heart-]base.
The physical basis is a condition for the clung-to aggregates by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*).
Subsequently arisen—both clung-to aggregates and the non-clung-to edible food—are conditions for this clung-to body by way of presence-condition.
Subsequently arisen—non-clung-to aggregates and the material life-faculty—are conditions for the kamma-produced matter by way of presence-condition.
States, both clung-to (*upādinna*) and not-clung-to (*anupādinna*), are related to a state that is not-clung-to by way of presence condition (*atthipaccaya*):

namely, conascence (*sahajāta*), prenascence (*purejāta*), postnascence (*pacchājāta*), and nutriment (*āhāra*). As conascence: Clung-to aggregates and great primaries are related to mind-produced matter by way of presence condition.
As conascence: One not-clung-to aggregate and the [heart-]base are related to the three...
The aggregates are related to [the aggregates] by way of presence condition …pe… two aggregates …pe….

As pre-nascence: the non-clung-to visible-base and the [heart-]base are related to the non-clung-to aggregates by way of presence condition …pe… the tangible-base and the [heart-]base are related to the non-clung-to aggregates by way of presence condition. As post-nascence: the clung-to aggregates …pe….
And non-clung-to edible food is a condition, by way of presence-condition, for this non-clung-to body.
Clung-to and non-clung-to states are a condition, by way of presence-condition, for clung-to and non-clung-to states.
[Regarding] nutriment: clung-to and non-clung-to edible food is a condition for this clung-to...
And it is a condition for the unclung-to body by way of presence-condition (*atthipaccaya*),
absence-condition (*natthipaccaya*), disappearance-condition (*vigatapaccaya*), and non-disappearance-condition (*avigatapaccaya*).
Chapter on Enumeration.
In the pure root condition there are four; in the object condition, four; in the predominance condition, two; in the proximity condition, four; in the contiguity condition, four;

in the conascence condition, five; in the mutuality condition, two; in the support condition, five; in the decisive support condition, four; in the prenascence condition, six; in the postnascence condition...
Six; in relation to repetition, one; in relation to kamma, five; in relation to result, four; in relation to nutriment, nine; in relation to faculty, four;
in relation to jhāna, four; in relation to path, four; in relation to association, two; in relation to dissociation, six; in relation to presence, nine; in relation to absence, four;
in relation to disappearance, four; in relation to non-disappearance, nine.
The Negative Extraction:
A state that is clung-to (upādinna) is a condition for a state that is clung-to by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya),

Condition ... by way of nutriment-condition ... by way of faculty-condition.

Condition ... by way of nutriment-condition.

A clung-to state is a condition, by way of conascence-condition and by way of postnascence-condition, for a state that is both clung-to and not-clung-to; [it is also] a condition by way of nutriment-condition.
A not-clung-to state is a condition, by way of object-condition and by way of conascence-condition, for a not-clung-to state.
Conditioned relation: ... by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*) ... by way of postnascence condition (*pacchājāta-paccaya*) ...

by way of nutriment condition (*āhāra-paccaya*). A state not acquired by clinging (*anupādinnadhamma*) is a condition for a state acquired by clinging (*upādinnadhamma*) by way of object condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*), by way of decisive support condition, by way of postnascence condition, by way of kamma condition (*kamma-paccaya*), and by way of nutriment condition.
A state not acquired by clinging is a condition for both a state acquired by clinging and a state not acquired by clinging by way of postnascence condition and by way of nutriment condition.
States that are both clung-to and not clung-to are related to a state that is clung-to by way of prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty conditions.
States that are both clung-to and not clung-to are related to a state that is not clung-to by way of conascence, prenascence, postnascence, and nutriment conditions.
States that are both clung-to and not clung-to are related to a state that is both clung-to and not clung-to by way of the nutriment condition.
2.10.14.7.2. Pure Enumeration Chapter on the Negative Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīya Saṅkhyāvāra Suddha)

With not-root condition, nine; with not-object condition, nine (nine in all cases); with not-nutriment condition, eight … pe … with not-association condition, nine; with not-dissociation condition, nine; with not-presence condition, four; with not-absence condition, nine;

with not-disappearance condition, nine; with not-non-disappearance condition, four. 2.10.14.7.3. With non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are four [answers] for object (ārammaṇa), two for predominance (adhipati) [the positive matrix should be made here] … pe … nine for non-disappearance (avigata).
